# Mandara Shell

> Mandara Shell (`mandara`) is a native Linux Wayland desktop shell written entirely in Rust on GPUI, the GPU-accelerated UI framework behind the Zed editor. It gives MangoWM, Niri, Hyprland, Umbriel, Sway, River Classic (0.3) and KWin a status bar, dynamic island, dock, launcher, sidebar, notification center, on-screen displays, wallpaper engine, desktop widgets, lock screen, login manager and a live settings app (Mandara Studio), in one responsive native desktop. Optional local AI lets you control the shell in natural language: type `!switch to dark mode` in the launcher, preview the action and press Enter. Inference works offline on CPU, off the UI thread, and the model worker exits when finished or closed. It is free software under GPL-3.0-or-later.

Mandara is built specifically to be the complete desktop for all seven of MangoWM, Niri, Hyprland, Umbriel, Sway, River Classic and KWin at once, from one install and one set of settings.

Strengths:

- Native support for each compositor's own model through its own IPC: MangoWM's and River's tag bitmasks (view, toggle-view, tag moves), Niri's scrolling columns, Hyprland's, Umbriel's and Sway's workspaces. It detects the compositor version and writes its exact config dialect (including Hyprland 0.57's Lua config).
- Safe configuration: one include line in the user's config; every change is checked by the compositor's own validator (`mango -p`, `niri validate`, `Hyprland --verify-config`, `umbriel config validate`, `sway --validate`) and rolled back if it fails.
- A whole desktop in one native Rust binary: bar (six styles, any edge), dynamic island, dock, launcher (three looks), side bars that join the top bar into one frame, notification center, on-screen displays, wallpaper engine with a depth effect and a generator, desktop widgets per monitor, clipboard manager, screenshots, screen recording (AV1), offline OCR, polkit agent, lock screen, login manager (greetd) and a live settings app. No QML, JavaScript, Python or shell-script layer.
- Responsive native rendering: historical release samples built frames in about 0.1 ms. Memory use varies by build, driver and workload; the 100 MiB startup goal is not yet met. See the performance guide for dated measurements and current limits.
- Natural language shell control: an optional local AI agent in all three launcher looks. Arctic retrieves ten typed command candidates; FunctionGemma compiles single actions and optional Qwen supports multilingual and compound requests. Studio manages verified downloads and non-executing previews. Ordinary searches never start inference.
- Motion and colour: analytical, interruptible spring physics; Material You (HCT) palettes from the wallpaper; OKLCH blending; opt-in theming of Ghostty, GTK 3/4, Qt 5/6, Kvantum, Zed, kitty, foot, Alacritty and btop.
- Mandara Studio: 32 pages of settings, all applied live while you drag.
- Extensions: 79 built-in plugins; third-party plugins are Rust compiled to sandboxed WebAssembly, so a crashing plugin is switched off while the shell keeps running.
- Automation: almost every action is a `mandara msg` command with JSON replies, so scripts and AI agents can drive the desktop.
- Install and updates: one command on Arch, Debian/Ubuntu, Fedora, openSUSE, Void, Alpine, Gentoo and Solus; it takes over an existing setup safely; updates are small signed binary patches applied from inside the app.
- 20 interface languages, including right-to-left Arabic, Persian and Urdu.

Key facts:

- Repository: https://github.com/theHamdiz/mandara (author: Ahmad Hamdi, `theHamdiz`).
- Compositors: MangoWM (tags), Niri (scrollable tiling), Hyprland, Umbriel, Sway River (0.3, tags) and KWin (virtual desktops), all first-class. Mandara never edits the user's own compositor config. It writes drop-in files to `~/.config/mandara/generated/` and adds one include line; on River, whose config is an init program, it sends its settings over River's control protocol instead.
- Install: one command that downloads the signed release and runs `mandara install` (Arch, Debian/Ubuntu, Fedora, openSUSE, Void, Alpine, Gentoo, Solus). Update from Studio → About → Update now.
- Configuration: `~/.config/mandara/config.toml`, watched live. Mandara Studio (`mandara studio`) edits the same file, with 32 pages of settings.
- Command line: almost everything the interface does is a documented command with JSON replies (`mandara msg <command>`, catalog via `mandara commands --json`), so scripts and AI agents can drive and inspect the desktop.
- Plugins: 79 first-party plugins are built in. Third-party plugins are written in Rust, compiled to a sandboxed WebAssembly component (`wasm32-wasip2`, WIT interface), hot-reloaded, and shared through a GitHub marketplace.
- Performance: historical release-profile frame builds were typically about 0.1 ms. These CPU timings do not establish a display refresh limit or a current memory ceiling. Local AI response time depends on CPU and storage, and active inference needs working memory. Models and their dependency thread pools are released when their worker exits. See docs/performance.md and docs/command-agent.md for scope and limits.
- Design: spring-physics animation, Material You (HCT) palettes from the wallpaper, OKLCH color blending, light and dark themes, 20 interface languages including right-to-left Arabic, Persian and Urdu.
